title: QA Engineer III (Internal Systems)
description:
QA ENGINEER III (INTERNAL SYSTEMS)

Level: P3 | QA Engineer III (Senior)
Location: Remote | Canada
Reports To: Tyler Chandler de Faye | Associate Manager, Operations & Efficiency https://www.linkedin.com/in/tyler-chandler-de-faye/
Type: Permanent | Full-Time




ABOUT SOLINK

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 36,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!




THE ROLE

As a QA Engineer III (Internal Systems), you’ll play a hands-on role in solving meaningful problems, driving outcomes, and contributing directly to Solink’s growth. You'll collaborate across teams and be trusted to take ownership - because we believe great ideas come from everywhere.

You’ll own quality for Solink’s internal tools, starting with our Salesforce platform and the systems connected to it and growing to the other tools and automations our teams rely on: you’ll set the test strategy, build the test automation, and decide when a release is ready.

This is an opportunity for someone who’s energized by challenge, fast learning, and making a real impact.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own test strategy for Salesforce and, over time, our other internal tools: coverage goals, the mix of test types, our regression approach, and which tests to automate now, automate once a feature is stable, or keep manual by design.

 - Choose and build our test automation framework, starting with Salesforce and designed to extend to other internal tools, including tooling, test data model and reporting, and add automated quality gates to our deploy pipeline.

 - Build and maintain an automated regression suite for our highest-risk processes (quote configurator, Opportunity close to Work Order, Work Order lines to billing, and access by persona), and add a test whenever a bug reaches production or a process changes.

 - Design and run test cases for Salesforce changes (flows, validation rules, Apex, Lightning pages, permissions and the quote configurator), each with a persona, test data, steps and an expected result, covering edge cases, negative paths and boundary conditions, prioritized by risk.

 - Test as the real user, not as an admin, and run regression checks before anything reaches production so we know what a change should do and what it must not touch.

 - Check every change for downstream impact on connected systems (NetSuite, Solink Manage/CallHome, Ironclad, HubSpot): know which fields each integration reads and writes, test as the integration user, and confirm the first sync after release.

 - Extend test coverage beyond Salesforce to our other internal tools and automations, such as n8n workflows, Google Apps Script tools, Slack integrations and AI agents, as they take on business-critical work.

 - Run regression testing for Salesforce's three seasonal releases (Spring, Summer, Winter): review the release notes and upcoming release updates for anything that affects the org, run the regression suite in a preview sandbox before the Prod upgrade, and log issues in SPI ahead of the upgrade date.

 - Make the release-readiness call for production deploys based on test evidence and customer impact, and lead defect triage when a high-risk release goes wrong.

 - Support SPI (Salesforce Platform & Integrations) intake: review new issues, check each against the live org (permissions first, then regression or other causes), group issues with the same root cause, and co-author acceptance criteria so issues are ready for development with reproduction steps and the right approver tagged.

 - Own bug handling: reproduce, document and route bugs in SPI, retest fixes, record the result on the ticket, and close the test gap behind repeat failures.

 - Plan and run UAT with business testers: seed their test records, record Pass, Fail or Blocked with evidence, and turn feedback into clear findings.

 - Raise the bar for the developers who ship changes to Salesforce and our internal tools: review their Apex tests and acceptance criteria, and help build quality in from design rather than after implementation.

 - Use AI tools to speed up test design, test data setup and investigation, and verify AI-generated tests and diagnoses rather than taking them at face value.




WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Have:

 - 5+ years in QA, including designing and building a test automation framework, not only adding tests to an existing one.

 - Deep expertise in at least one automation language or framework, and experience testing across UI, API and integration layers.

 - Experience running automated tests as quality gates in a CI/CD pipeline.

 - Hands-on Salesforce experience (objects, fields, record pages, flows, validation rules, profiles and permission sets) and the ability to tell a permission problem from a logic problem.

 - Comfortable picking up a new internal tool quickly and working out how to test it, including tools with no existing tests or documentation.

 - Strong investigation habits and clear writing: you reproduce first, verify root causes yourself, document what you see, and can explain a failure to a salesperson, an ops lead and a developer.

 - Working knowledge of Jira: writing tickets, linking related issues, keeping statuses and comments accurate.

Nice-to-Have:

 - Salesforce test automation tools such as Provar, Copado Robotic Testing, or Playwright or Selenium against Lightning.

 - Experience with Apex test classes, Flow tests, SOQL or the Salesforce CLI.

 - Experience testing integrations between Salesforce and ERP, marketing or contract systems, or testing REST APIs directly.

 - Experience testing workflow automation or low-code tools such as n8n, Zapier or Google Apps Script, or testing AI-driven automations.

 - Experience running UAT with non-technical testers.

 - Salesforce Administrator certification, or willingness to earn it in your first year.




CAREER ARCHETYPE ROLE EXPECTATIONS

Career archetypes represent the foundational behaviours and performance standards expected of every employee, regardless of role or level.

At Solink, career archetypes define the baseline for how we show up and create impact. They are not aspirational traits or optional strengths, they are the minimum standards required to operate successfully within our environment. These expectations ensure consistency in how we think, collaborate, execute, and raise the performance bar. If someone consistently does not meet these standards, they are not aligned with what it takes to thrive at Solink.

This is a P3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level are drivers who own initiatives end-to-end with very little direction, propose and launch initiatives, and clearly articulate the root cause of a problem along with a thought-through solution.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

 - Own quality for Salesforce and our other internal tools end-to-end, escalating early when something is unclear or risky.

 - Make quality gate decisions from test evidence and customer impact, not schedule pressure, and say plainly what was and was not tested.

 - Handle access and data with care: use sandboxes, never touch production data without sign-off, and clean up after testing.

 - Keep every ticket self-contained so someone who was not there can follow what happened and why.

 - Raise the bar for the team by turning repeat defects into automated tests, clearer "ready for development" standards and better guardrails.

 - Treat the regression suite as a living asset: every escaped bug becomes a test case, and nothing reaches production without the relevant tests being run.

 - Share testing practice with developers and business testers through reviews, pairing and informal mentoring.
   
   


SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

 - Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.
   
   


COMPENSATION

The salary range for this role is $86,203 - $102,366 CAD. We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role. For this position, we are hiring within the P3 range. Candidates in this range will demonstrate end-to-end ownership of quality, hands-on experience building test automation, clear root-cause analysis, and the judgment to make release decisions from test evidence.




OUR VALUES

We do things the Solink way:

 - Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.

 - Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.

 - Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.

 - Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.




WHY SOLINK?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

 - Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.

 - Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.

 - Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.

 - Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.

 - Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.

 - Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.

 - Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.
   
   


WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE HIRING PROCESS

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

 1. Intro call with our Talent Team

 2. Interview with the Hiring Manager

 3. Role-relevant task or case (if applicable)

 4. Final interviews with cross-functional team members

 5. Reference Checks

 6. Offer & onboarding 🎉


PLEASE NOTE: THIS IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE AT ANY POINT IN THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THE BUSINESS.




HOW TO APPLY

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our Careers Page https://solink.com/careers/. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.




NOTICE: SOLINK USES ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TO SCREEN, ASSESS, AND/OR SELECT CANDIDATES FOR THIS POSITION.




SOLINK IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER. WE’RE COMMITTED TO BUILDING A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE WORKPLACE. IF YOU REQUIRE ACCOMMODATION DURING THE SELECTION PROCESS, PLEASE LET US KNOW.
